title: What is known about 1RB0RF_1RC1LB_1LD1RE_1LB0LD_1RF0RC_1RA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RF_1RC1LB_1LD1RE_1LB0LD_1RF0RC_1RA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open, but the run is now understood up to its rebuilds. Between rebuilds the machine is a binary counter that applies one fixed operation to a list of blocks once per tick, and the list is the binary expansion of the time it has left (checked against the machine, not proved). Rebuilds are simulated cell by cell. With this the run passes 1,503 rebuilds, more than 103,739 steps, without a halt (before: 109 steps).

Same skeleton as a sibling. The machine 1RB0RE_0RC0RF_1LD1RA_1RE0LD_0LB1RC_1LE--- follows the same model with blocks of 3a + 2 cells instead of 2a + 1. There, tapes of the machine's own shape halt; here none was found, and the rebuilds have no rule yet.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 203 cells have been visited and 70 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Three rounds of the run, for any tape further left
claims.text: Three consecutive rounds of the run from blank tape (between moments the head is in C on the first 0 right of everything written), each proved for every tape left of the cells it visits, with its exact step count.

claims.title: Doubling rounds
claims.text: No halt in 10<sup>9</sup> steps. Between consecutive moments the head is in C at the right end on a pure block tape the last block grows by 5; from step 3·10<sup>5</sup> on each round takes twice the time of the one before plus a small constant c (c = 5 or 9 during a walk, between −55 and 33 when the list is rebuilt).

claims.title: Between rebuilds: a binary counter that applies one list operation per tick
claims.text: The same model as for the sibling 1RB0RE_0RC0RF_1LD1RA_1RE0LD_0LB1RC_1LE---, in another coding. At the moments the head is in C on a 0 just right of a 1, the tape is a list of blocks of 1s separated by single 0s (the interior), then a block of one 1, a last block l, and to the right of the head a zone of single 1s. Call it regular if the first block is even, the other interior blocks are odd, l is a positive multiple of 5, and the gaps of the zone are 0 mod 5 (the first, counted from the head) and 4 mod 5 (the others). From one such moment to the next (a sub-round) the interior takes one step W: (..., x, 2a + 1) becomes (..., x + 2, 1, ..., 1) with a blocks of 1. The last block and the zone are a binary counter: with segments s1 = g1, si = gi + 1, a last block l > 5 becomes a new first segment l − 5 and l = 5; with l = 5 the n leading segments equal to 5 are removed, the next segment loses 5 cells (blank tape supplies them if there is none) and l = 5n + 10. So l plus the segments is 5(m + 1) for 2m sub-rounds (one round), then m grows by 1. Checked against the machine one sub-round at a time: of the 400,000 sub-rounds after step 1,399 (16 million steps) the 399,965 regular ones all follow this; the other 35 are the transient of the first rebuild. Observed and checked, not proved.

claims.title: The list is the binary expansion of the time it has left
claims.text: With digits ai = (bi − 1)/2, W removes the last digit a, adds 1 to the digit before it and appends a zeros. A tail (..., q, a) becomes (..., q + a + 1) after exactly 2a steps, so an interior with digits a1, ..., ak is a single block after exactly T = Σi 2ai + ... + ak + k − i steps of W. (This is arithmetic on the rule W, not on the machine.) Checked on the machine: the model predicts the single block at sub-round 7,964 of that run and it is there; and after the first rebuild the lists at six ends of rounds, up to step 1.07·1010, are those of a direct run of the machine (2 1^7 3 1^3 7 1^10 7 3 1^4 | 1 | 120 at step 335,864,993, ..., 2 1^6 3 15 1^10 7 3 1^4 | 1 | 145 at step 10,737,738,872).

claims.title: 1,503 rebuilds without a halt
claims.text: A run that takes the regular sub-rounds by arithmetic (any number at once, with the two rules above) and gives everything else to the machine itself, cell by cell: the transient after each single block. It passes 1,503 rebuilds; by then the counter has made more than 2<sup>12,424</sup> sub-rounds, so the machine more than 10<sup>3,739</sup> steps. A halt could only be found by the direct part and none was. The arithmetic part rests on the two rules above for all sizes, which are checked, not proved. The run stops there for a practical reason: the transient after the 1,504th single block (25,096 cells) contains a second kind of regular stretch, in which the block before the last one is 2l/5 + 1 instead of 1 and a gap of the zone that is 4 mod 5 is used up 5 cells at a time. The model does not cover it yet and simulating it cell by cell takes too long.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Between rebuilds the machine cannot halt if the model is right; what the transient of a rebuild does has no rule yet, and a second kind of regular stretch inside the transients is not modelled. The sibling 1RB0RE_0RC0RF_1LD1RA_1RE0LD_0LB1RC_1LE---, which follows the same model, has tapes of its own shape that halt, so the shape alone is unlikely to decide this machine either.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Between its rebuilds this machine is a binary counter that applies one small operation to a list of blocks at every tick, and the list is, read in binary, the time left until the next rebuild. This page runs the machine, lets you step the list and the counter, and lists what is known.

facts.text: No halt, more than 10<sup>3,739</sup> steps (model checked, not proved).
The model against the machine, one sub-round at a time.
Rounds of the run proved in Lean for any tape further left.

sections.heading: A binary counter that rewrites a list
html: Stop the machine each time the head is in state C on a 0 just right of a 1. The tape is then a list of blocks of 1s separated by single 0s, a block of one 1, a last block, and right of the head a zone of single 1s. From one such moment to the next (a sub-round) two things happen, and they do not influence each other.

The list takes one step. Its last block, of 2a + 1 cells, gives 2 cells to the block on its left and falls apart into a blocks of 1: x, 2a+1 becomes x+2, 1, ..., 1. Counting a block of 2a + 1 as the digit a: the last digit a is removed, the digit before it grows by 1, and a zeros are appended.

The counter ticks. The last block and the zone hold a binary counter. A round is 2m sub-rounds in which they fill 5(m + 1) cells; then the last block is 5(m + 2) cells and round m + 1 starts. This is why each round takes twice as long as the one before.

The list gets shorter in the end, and how long that takes can be read off it: a list with digits a1, ..., ak is a single block after exactly T steps, where T has a binary 1 at the positions ak, ak + ak−1 + 1, ak + ak−1 + ak−2 + 2, and so on. The list is the time it has left, written in binary. Try it:

The start values are the tape at step 1,399 from blank tape (last block 15, so round 2). All of this was read off the run and then checked against the machine: 399,965 regular sub-rounds one by one and the lists at six round ends up to step 1.07·1010. It is not proved.

Rebuilds. When a single block is left, the sub-rounds are irregular for a while: the block is cut into 2 1 1 1 ..., cells of the last block and the zone move into the list, and then the regular life starts again with a longer list. No rule is known for this part; the long run simulates it cell by cell. The first rebuilds:

sections.heading: Why it is hard to settle
html: The machine halts only in state F reading a 1. In a regular sub-round that does not happen (in the model). What the irregular stretch after a single block does has no rule yet. For the sibling 1RB0RE_0RC0RF_1LD1RA_1RE0LD_0LB1RC_1LE---, which follows the same model in another coding, some tapes of the machine's own shape halt; for this machine a search over small single blocks found none.

The run from blank tape has passed 1,503 rebuilds, more than 103,739 steps, without a halt. After that the irregular stretches contain a second kind of regular behaviour that is not modelled yet, and the run cannot be followed further for now.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.04).
After 109 steps the tape spans 203 cells (6 left of the start, 191 right), with a density of 1s of 0.345.

The tape (run-length coded, 1^5 is five 1s, C>0 the head in state C on a 0) at some of the last moments the head reached a new cell, cut to 400 characters:

family: two-level block counter (fast tail, walking block in a unary list)
summary: Binary counter applying one list operation W per tick; the block list is the binary expansion of the time to the next rebuild (checked, not proved); rebuild transients simulated directly; no halt in 1,503 rebuilds (more than 10^3,739 steps); open.
